principle: Preserve every capability, use each at its strongest phase, and keep only the current phase active.

resources.name: awesome-design-md
resources.use_when: A product needs a design archetype, component language, visual benchmark, or product-specific DESIGN.md.
resources.do_not: Do not copy protected logos, proprietary fonts, imagery, screenshots, or another company's trade dress.
resources.notes: The 73-company design-intelligence synthesis and design-system routing.

resources.name: Perplexity AI GitHub organisation
resources.use_when: An agent needs current patterns for research tooling, evaluation runners, safe binary distribution, or developer-tool inventory.
resources.do_not: Do not assume every public repository in an organisation has the same licence.
resources.notes: Research extension, resumable evals, content-addressed records, self-tests, and safe installers.

resources.name: api-platform-developers
resources.use_when: The project needs official Perplexity Agent Skills, a Claude/Codex plugin example, or live documentation through MCP.
resources.do_not: Do not make Perplexity credentials or the docs MCP mandatory for Escapement core.
resources.notes: Portable skills, plugin manifests, optional docs MCP, and an official research extension.

resources.name: pplx CLI
resources.license: No licence file observed during review
resources.use_when: A user explicitly wants Perplexity-backed current web search or snippets and can provide an API key.
resources.do_not: Do not copy repository code into Escapement or claim open-source reuse until a licence is present and verified.
resources.notes: Checksum-verified releases, atomic updates, JSON stdout, and agent-friendly CLI design.

resources.name: search_evals
resources.use_when: Escapement needs reproducible eval suites, provider adapters, task traces, resumable runs, or cost/evidence accounting.
resources.do_not: Do not import paid-provider assumptions or third-party benchmark data without accepting their separate terms.
resources.notes: Resumable executable evaluations and inspectable per-task traces.

resources.name: Bumblebee
resources.use_when: A security review needs read-only package, skill, editor-extension, or MCP inventory from local metadata.
resources.do_not: Do not expose credentials found in MCP env blocks or broaden scans beyond approved roots.
resources.notes: Read-only inventory profiles, structured NDJSON, confidence levels, and built-in self-test.

resources.name: Perplexity MCP server
resources.use_when: A project wants Perplexity search through MCP rather than a CLI.
resources.do_not: Do not register remote MCP servers silently or make network access part of the default core.
resources.notes: Optional freshness and research integrations through a narrow MCP boundary.

resources.name: Codescythe
resources.use_when: A TypeScript or JavaScript repository needs deterministic dead-code analysis or dependency-path explanation.
resources.do_not: Do not run destructive fixes without a clean branch, tests, and explicit approval.
resources.notes: Narrow deterministic contracts, doctor commands, explainability, and safe destructive-mode gates.

resources.name: AppFlowy
resources.use_when: Designing local-first state, user-owned data, extensible workspace architecture, or self-hosted collaboration.
resources.do_not: Do not copy AGPL code into Escapement's source-available core without a deliberate licence decision.
resources.notes: Privacy-first local control, cross-platform reliability, and extensible building blocks.

resources.name: Plausible Analytics
resources.use_when: Designing privacy-first observability, minimal dashboards, transparent metrics, or optional self-hosted analytics.
resources.do_not: Do not embed AGPL application code into Escapement core without licence review.
resources.notes: Local-only telemetry by default, transparent metrics, and clutter-free observability.

resources.name: Spec Kit
resources.use_when: New or material work needs a constitution, executable specification, technical plan, task breakdown, or convergence review.
resources.do_not: Do not duplicate its whole command surface in Escapement when an optional integration is sufficient.
resources.notes: Constitution → specify → plan → tasks → implement → converge, plus extensions, presets, and bundles.

resources.name: 500+ AI Agent Projects & Use Cases
resources.use_when: An agent needs to discover relevant implementation patterns or comparable industry use cases.
resources.do_not: Do not treat inclusion in a catalogue as proof of safety, quality, maintenance, or licence compatibility.
resources.notes: A curated agent-pattern registry rather than hundreds of always-loaded agents.

resources.name: Learn Harness Engineering
resources.use_when: Creating, assessing, or teaching the instructions, tools, environment, state, and feedback subsystems of a harness.
resources.do_not: Do not load the complete course into every task or confuse a prompt file with a complete harness.
resources.notes: Repository as system of record, feature-state primitives, lifecycle bootstrap, verification, and clean session closure.

resources.name: harness-creator skill
resources.use_when: A project lacks a harness or needs a structured five-subsystem assessment.
resources.do_not: Do not install it on top of overlapping native Escapement harness skills without an overlap decision.
resources.notes: Harness assessment, templates, reference patterns, and benchmark-oriented skill development.

resources.name: Penpot
resources.use_when: A product needs open design tokens, inspectable design-to-code workflows, or an optional design MCP/API.
resources.do_not: Do not copy branding or assume a design file alone proves implementation correctness.
resources.notes: Design tokens as shared source of truth and programmable design-code integration.

resources.name: HelixDB
resources.use_when: A project genuinely needs graph-vector memory, knowledge graphs, or a local agent data layer.
resources.do_not: Do not make a database mandatory for Escapement's file-based core or add it merely to appear agentic.
resources.notes: A guided one-shot bootstrap and optional structured memory backend.

resources.name: Agent Reach
resources.use_when: A user explicitly needs internet/platform access not already available through approved tools.
resources.do_not: Do not bypass platform protections, harvest credentials, or install broad internet capabilities without explicit approval.
resources.notes: Capability doctor, safe mode, fallback routing, and agent-friendly configuration.

resources.name: agent-browser
resources.use_when: A frontend or end-to-end task needs real browser evidence, accessibility-tree interaction, screenshots, or DOM inspection.
resources.do_not: Do not browse authenticated or sensitive sites without approval or use browser automation as proof when business data is fabricated.
resources.notes: Agent-readable accessibility snapshots, early interaction failure, and browser-based verification.

resources.name: GSD Core
resources.use_when: A project needs phase-level context isolation, fresh execution contexts, or a discuss-plan-execute-verify-ship loop.
resources.do_not: Do not run parallel agents when tasks share mutable state or when the repository lacks merge and verification controls.
resources.notes: Fresh-context phase execution, lean main sessions, and verified shipping.

resources.name: mcp-builder skill
resources.use_when: A project is approved to build an MCP server for an external API or service.
resources.do_not: Do not expose broad destructive endpoints, secrets, or an unbounded API surface to agents.
resources.notes: MCP quality workflow, tool discoverability, output schemas, annotations, and realistic evaluations.

resources.name: find-skills skill
resources.use_when: A task requires a specialised capability that Escapement core does not own.
resources.do_not: Do not recommend or install a skill solely because it ranks highly or has many installs.
resources.notes: Reference-router skill and a quality gate before external skill installation.

resources.name: ECC
resources.use_when: Reviewing cross-runtime distribution, doctor/repair, installation conflict detection, skill packaging, or harness security.
resources.do_not: Do not copy its hundreds of agents/skills into Escapement core or imply full platform parity.
resources.notes: Doctor/repair, official-source warning, install-conflict prevention, security scanning, and support matrix honesty.

resources.name: Strix
resources.use_when: The user has explicit authorisation to dynamically assess a local, owned, or approved target in a sandbox.
resources.do_not: Do not autonomously attack public or third-party targets, run exploits without permission, or place offensive capability in Escapement core.
resources.notes: Local run viewer, evidence-rich findings, CI security gates, and sandboxed external security integrations.

resources.name: Stop Slop
resources.use_when: A complete human-facing draft needs a final anti-slop pass after content and judgement are correct.
resources.do_not: Do not load for code-only work or use it as a substitute for substantive writing.

resources.name: Task Observer
resources.license: Attribution-required open licence; verify current file
resources.use_when: A long-running project wants to observe repeated task patterns and propose candidate skills.
resources.do_not: Do not let it modify skills automatically or observe sensitive sessions without approval.

resources.name: Taste Skill
resources.use_when: A frontend project needs a strong external design director with adjustable variance, motion, and density.
resources.do_not: Do not load alongside Impeccable or Open Design as a second full design director.

resources.name: Open Design
resources.use_when: A project needs a local-first design workspace, broad design-skill suite, or artifact-first design workflow.
resources.do_not: Do not install the full platform merely for a small UI review or combine it with another full design suite.

resources.name: Emil Kowalski Design Skills
resources.use_when: A UI needs specialised motion judgement or animation review.
resources.do_not: Do not use motion to compensate for weak hierarchy or load the full suite for static enterprise screens.

resources.name: Impeccable
resources.use_when: A frontend needs one comprehensive design skill plus deterministic anti-pattern checks.
resources.do_not: Do not load with Taste Skill or Open Design as a second primary design director.

resources.name: Superpowers
resources.use_when: A team explicitly wants the Superpowers methodology for development execution.
resources.do_not: Do not combine its full lifecycle hooks with ECC or GSD without an overlap decision.

resources.name: Claude Mem
resources.license: AGPL-3.0 for main package; verify subcomponents
resources.use_when: Local file handoffs are insufficient and the project accepts a background memory service and its licence.
resources.do_not: Do not install by default, duplicate Escapement state, or capture confidential sessions without a privacy decision.

resources.name: Graphify
resources.use_when: A large or heterogeneous repository needs deterministic relationship mapping beyond ordinary file search.
resources.do_not: Do not index sensitive material through external backends without approval or use it for a small codebase.

resources.name: gstack
resources.use_when: A project explicitly wants role-based plan reviews or fresh-context specialist reviews.
resources.do_not: Do not install its full workflow alongside Superpowers or ECC without deciding which system owns orchestration.

resources.name: Everything Claude Code / ECC
resources.use_when: A user wants ECC components or profiles that Escapement does not provide.
resources.do_not: Do not install the full profile on top of Escapement hooks and native skills; use component-level selection.

resources.name: Context7
resources.use_when: Implementation depends on current external library documentation.
resources.do_not: Do not use it as the source of truth for the project's own code or business rules.

resources.name: Last30Days
resources.use_when: A decision benefits from recent community signals rather than only authoritative documentation.
resources.do_not: Do not use social discourse as authoritative evidence or load it for stable facts.

resources.name: Skill UI
resources.use_when: Retained from the original capability set pending exact source confirmation.
resources.do_not: Do not install or attribute this entry until the exact repository is confirmed.

resources.name: Claude Code Review
resources.use_when: A supported organisation wants Anthropic's managed PR review service.
resources.do_not: Do not present it as open source or use it in addition to another expensive full review workflow without reason.

resources.name: Ponytail
resources.use_when: An agent repeatedly overbuilds bounded implementation tasks.
resources.do_not: Do not let minimalism remove validation, security, observability, or approved requirements.

resources.name: Mobbin
resources.use_when: A designer needs real-product interaction and screen references.
resources.do_not: Do not scrape, redistribute, or copy protected screens and assets.

resources.name: Refero
resources.use_when: A product needs curated web and product references.
resources.do_not: Do not copy protected layouts or assets as trade dress.

resources.name: Recent
resources.use_when: A task needs a current design-reference shortlist.
resources.do_not: Do not let trend references override brand, usability, or enterprise density.

resources.name: 21st.dev
resources.use_when: A project needs a component starting point compatible with its stack.
resources.do_not: Do not introduce copied components without licence, dependency, accessibility, and design-system review.

resources.name: shadcn/ui
resources.use_when: A React project explicitly chooses shadcn/ui as its component foundation.
resources.do_not: Do not add it to a project with an established incompatible component system.

resources.name: GSAP
resources.license: GSAP standard licence; verify current terms
resources.use_when: The approved interaction genuinely requires advanced timeline or scroll animation.
resources.do_not: Do not add it for ordinary transitions or without dependency and licence review.

resources.name: Headroom.js
resources.use_when: A product specifically needs scroll-aware header behaviour.
resources.do_not: Do not add a dependency when a small native implementation already exists and is tested.

resources.name: Playwright
resources.use_when: A project needs robust browser automation and either already uses Playwright or approves it.
resources.do_not: Do not install it solely for a tiny static inspection.

resources.name: Andrej Karpathy Coding Guidelines
resources.publisher: forrestchang / derived from Andrej Karpathy observations
resources.use_when: Engineering work needs explicit assumptions, simplicity, surgical changes and verifiable goals.
resources.do_not: Do not duplicate the same guidance through another always-loaded minimalism rule.

resources.name: UI/UX Pro Max
resources.license: Repository reports MIT; CLI materials may differ. Verify selected release and component.
resources.use_when: A UI task benefits from searchable product-type, style, palette, typography, UX, chart or stack recommendations.
resources.do_not: Do not let generated recommendations override DESIGN.md or the design intelligence constitution.

resources.name: Anthropic Frontend Design
resources.use_when: An approved design specification needs production-grade frontend implementation.
resources.do_not: Do not use as the design constitution or alongside multiple primary art-direction systems.

resources.name: Playwright MCP
resources.use_when: Exploratory or long-running agent browser loops benefit from persistent accessibility-tree state.
resources.do_not: Do not prefer MCP over CLI or project tests when token efficiency and deterministic test code are more important.

resources.name: Stagehand
resources.use_when: Production browser automation needs a controlled blend of code, natural language, caching and self-healing.
resources.do_not: Do not add it for ordinary end-to-end tests or without reviewing network, model and credential requirements.

resources.name: Cypress
resources.use_when: The project already uses Cypress or explicitly selects it as the browser test framework.
resources.do_not: Do not introduce Cypress into a Playwright-based project without a migration reason.

resources.name: Puppeteer MCP Server
resources.use_when: An existing approved project depends on the archived Puppeteer MCP server and migration is not immediate.
resources.do_not: Do not select for new projects; prefer maintained Playwright CLI/MCP or project-native tests.

resources.name: Prime Agent
triggers: run a long-lived background coding agent
resources.use_when: A project explicitly needs a separate long-running agent runtime, background or detachable sessions, persistent REPL execution, recursive subagents, or retained goals, schedules and heartbeats.
resources.do_not: Do not classify it as a skill, let it and Escapement co-own lifecycle phase, task state, memory, permissions, skill promotion, verification or closure, or describe its processes as a security sandbox.
resources.notes: A self-improving RLM coding-agent harness where sub-agents are function calls inside a persistent IPython kernel. A future adapter would have Escapement own specification, governance, approvals, evidence and closure, with Prime Agent as the approved execution host for a bounded task.

resources.name: Understand Anything
resources.use_when: Onboarding into a large or unfamiliar codebase, creating an architecture or dependency map, extracting business-domain flows, performing guided codebase tours, or analysing change impact -- when ordinary repository inspection is no longer sufficient.
resources.do_not: Do not run full indexing automatically, index confidential repositories without approval, enable automatic commit hooks without approval, or treat the generated graph as the only source of truth instead of supporting evidence.
resources.notes: The strongest immediate integration candidate in this batch. A multi-agent pipeline builds an interactive knowledge graph (.ua/knowledge-graph.json) and supports a local model provider for privacy or enterprise use. Disclose likely token, storage and processing cost before a full scan; prefer ordinary repository inspection for small projects.

resources.name: Evolver
resources.license: GPL-3.0-or-later for the current published release
triggers: auditable improvement to our agent workflow
resources.use_when: A project has meaningful runtime history, logs, repeated failure patterns, or closed-turn evidence (see scripts/harness_observability.py) that a self-improvement pass could act on.
resources.do_not: Do not allow automatic modification of AGENTS.md, automatic mutation of native skills, automatic edits to policy or project state, a continuous loop by default, or sending repository logs to a network service without approval. Do not copy GPL code into Escapement's source-available core without a deliberate licence decision.
resources.notes: A GEP (Genome Evolution Protocol)-powered self-evolution engine for AI agents (Genes, Capsules, Events). The publisher has announced that future releases will move from fully open source to source-available; already-published MIT/GPL-3.0 versions are unaffected. Evolver may propose; Escapement skill-governance owns review, testing, approval, promotion and retirement -- the same META_OBSERVER relation as Task Observer.

resources.name: Agency Agents
resources.use_when: Identifying a missing specialist reviewer, drafting a fresh-context agent contract, comparing role definitions, or discovering deliverable structures.
resources.do_not: Do not install the complete roster, load multiple personas into a single phase, or treat personality wording or persona success metrics as verified expertise or independent evidence.
resources.notes: A large personality-driven persona library (engineering, design, marketing, product, GIS, game development, finance and more) with a companion desktop installer for several coding tools. Native Escapement skills remain the default; select one role at a time and convert it into a bounded input/output/evidence/stop-condition contract.

resources.name: Prompt Master
triggers: convert this approved specification into a
resources.use_when: A user wants an approved Escapement brief converted into a prompt for another tool: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, an image or video generation tool, n8n, Zapier, Make, or another specialised AI system.
resources.do_not: Do not make it part of every coding turn or let it replace Escapement-owned discovery, material questions, business or domain context, architecture decisions, approval gates, scope, acceptance criteria or verification requirements. Do not repeat unverified promotional claims such as zero wasted tokens, perfect prompt, universal accuracy or full memory retention.
resources.notes: A Claude Skill that carries prior decisions forward as a memory block and formats an approved brief for a target tool. Sequenced strictly after Escapement's own specification stage; Escapement continues to own discovery, decisions, specification and acceptance criteria.

resources.name: Matt Pocock Grilling / Grill Me
resources.use_when: The user explicitly asks to be grilled, stress-tested, or challenged on a plan or design before implementation begins.
resources.do_not: Do not activate implicitly for an ordinary feature request. Do not let it skip Escapement's own rules: inspect the repository before asking, ask no more than five material questions per round, always give a recommended default and consequence, and wait for confirmation before implementing.
resources.notes: grill-me is a thin wrapper; the substantive design-tree/question-frontier method lives in the grilling skill it calls. decision-coach remains the default and canonical skill for this overlap group -- this is an explicit intensifier, adapted with original wording as the Grilling Intensifier section of skills/decision-coach/SKILL.md, not an installed copy of the external skill text.

resources.name: Cloudflare OS
triggers: approval layer for agent side effects
resources.use_when: A task concerns agent workspace design, capability-based security, sandboxed AI-built apps, human approval of side-effecting actions, or narrow resource introduction to agents.
resources.do_not: Do not present it as a drop-in skill, add Cloudflare Workers dependencies to Escapement core, copy its full application architecture, or imply Escapement currently provides Cloudflare OS-style sandboxing or that Gatekeepers have been integrated rather than only referenced.
resources.notes: Open-sourced 2026-08-05. Capability-based Gatekeeper Worker mediation where credentials never reach the agent or agent-generated code. The code is Apache-2.0, but production runtime depends on Cloudflare Workers -- open source here does not mean portable.

resources.name: Graft
resources.use_when: A repository is large enough that agent context is expensive or imprecise, and a persistent code graph would cut tool calls and tokens.
resources.do_not: Do not repeat its published benchmark numbers as though they were reproduced here, and do not run it alongside Graphify or Understand Anything -- memory-and-knowledge is a SUBSTITUTE group.
resources.notes: Publishes a 162-run controlled efficiency benchmark and SWE-bench Verified results graded by the official harness. That paired vanilla-vs-augmented design is a reference implementation of the claim 3 method deferred in docs/decisions/ESCAPEMENT_BENCH_V1.md. No telemetry.

agents.name: Planner
agents.use_when: A material feature needs decomposition, dependencies, risks, and verification before implementation.
agents.promotion_rule: Keep as a pattern unless repeated evidence supports a dedicated native skill.

agents.name: Independent Evaluator
agents.use_when: Implementation needs assessment from a fresh context against explicit acceptance criteria.
agents.promotion_rule: Must use structured fixtures and deterministic evidence.

agents.name: Security Reviewer
agents.use_when: Auth, permissions, hooks, MCP, privacy, secrets, or deployment changes are material.
agents.promotion_rule: Offensive tools remain external and authorised-only.

agents.name: Browser Verifier
agents.use_when: A UI change needs accessibility-tree, interaction, screenshot, or responsive evidence.
agents.promotion_rule: Prefer an external pinned browser CLI over custom browser orchestration.

agents.name: Grounded Research Agent
agents.use_when: A task requires current external facts, primary-source discovery, or multi-step research.
agents.promotion_rule: Network access and credentials require approval.

agents.name: Workflow Analyst
agents.use_when: A process requires states, owners, exceptions, SLA, controls, and audit.
agents.promotion_rule: Business policy must come from approved sources, not agent inference.

agents.name: Dashboard Analyst
agents.use_when: Management needs traceable KPIs, drill-down, reconciliation, and decision support.
agents.promotion_rule: No metric is accepted without source and formula.

agents.name: Design System Architect
agents.use_when: A product needs tokens, components, design-code handoff, or a product DESIGN.md.
agents.promotion_rule: Client brand and accessibility take precedence.

agents.name: MCP Builder
agents.use_when: An approved external service should be exposed to agents through MCP.
agents.promotion_rule: Use explicit schemas, annotations, pagination, errors, and evals.

agents.name: Deterministic Cleanup Agent
agents.use_when: A repository needs dead-code or dependency cleanup with explainable proof.
agents.promotion_rule: Doctor and explain before destructive fix; verify after every cleanup pass.

agents.name: Memory Architect
agents.use_when: File-based state is insufficient and a project has a justified graph/vector memory requirement.
agents.promotion_rule: External storage is optional; file state remains the core default.

agents.name: Harness Optimizer
agents.use_when: Repeated failures show that instructions, tools, environment, state, or feedback need adjustment.
agents.promotion_rule: Every harness edit needs a predicted effect and a follow-up evaluation.

agents.name: Consulting Principal
agents.use_when: A material recommendation needs an independent management-outcome and implementation review.
agents.promotion_rule: Fresh-context review only; it does not own implementation.

agents.name: CTO Reviewer
agents.use_when: A product or architecture decision needs independent technical credibility, security, scale, and debt review.
agents.promotion_rule: Use only for material architecture or release decisions.

agents.name: Governance Reviewer
agents.use_when: A workflow or policy needs independent review of authority, controls, evidence, exceptions, and reporting.
agents.promotion_rule: Must cite approved policies or decisions.

agents.name: Artifact Editor
agents.use_when: A completed business artifact needs a fresh-context quality, structure, and style pass.
agents.promotion_rule: Editing only; it cannot change business facts or decisions.
